title: deletes_job survivor count is report-only; do not turn it back into a gate
answers: Why does mark_deletions_verified not fail when survivors are found?
deletes_job erasure requests never drain / stuck pending
Can I make the unswept_rows count block marking deletions verified?
body:
`mark_deletions_verified` in posthog/dags/deletes.py logs an error (`context.log.error`) and records `unswept_rows` metadata, but must never raise `dagster.Failure` on a non-zero or None count.
- Why: no branch of `_DELETE_PREDICATE` can use the primary key (each keys a dictionary on `team_id`), so the count on `events` reads the whole table and hits ClickHouse code 307 (read-bytes limit). Unknown is the ordinary outcome, and a larger budget does not help.
- Gating stalled every request in the run, and stranded requests grew the dictionaries the next count must read.
- A non-zero count is not proof of skipped work: team/event arms have no `inserted_at` bound, so stragglers can match.
- Safeguard against silent no-op sweeps lives upstream: `MutationRunner.reuse_since`.
- Only restore blocking after the count is narrowed to teams named in the dictionaries. See docs/internal/clickhouse-deletion-coverage.md ("The survivor count is a report, not a gate").
- Marking is not revisited: the adhoc tombstone keeps those uuids out of later runs.
